extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH NIAID R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a complete NIH R21 (NIAID) grant application (SF424/R&R + PHS 398 components) including research plan, biosketches, vertebrate animal sections, facilities/equipment descriptions, leadership plan, and resource-sharing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample may not reflect the latest format or rules; NIAID posts new samples periodically. Applicants must adhere to the specific Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) formatting and content requirements rather than relying solely on older sample applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF 424 (R&R) Face Page with required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all SF 424 (R&R) face page information including type of submission, federal identifier, applicant organizational DUNS, legal name and address, PI contact information, employer identification (EIN/TIN), type of applicant, proposed project start/end dates, descriptive project title, congressional district, and performance site information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural face page information is required for agency routing, certification, and administrative processing. Include organizational identifiers (DUNS, EIN), accurate PI/contact info, and performance site details. The face page also repeats keys used elsewhere (e.g., application type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, assurances, and authorized representative signature
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the authorized representative certifies the statements contained in the list of certifications and assurances and agrees to comply with resulting terms if an award is accepted; acknowledges legal penalties for false statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the authorized organizational representative signs and dates the application; include any required certification forms/attachments. False statements may have legal consequences (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract must summarize significance, aims, approach and expected outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise Project Summary/Abstract that explains the problem, scientific background, the research approach (including Aims), and the expected outcomes/impact of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows: brief background on Trypanosoma brucei, rationale for ribosome profiling, and explicit Aim 1 (establish technology/optimize conditions and bioinformatics pipeline) and Aim 2 (apply to pathogenic stage to identify translationally regulated genes). Use clear statements of aims and expected contributions to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative / Public Health Relevance Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short Project Narrative (Public Health Relevance Statement) that explains, in plain language, the public health problem and how the proposed research will address it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the statement concise and understandable to non-specialists. Example: explain disease burden, limitations of current treatments, and how the project will identify candidate drug targets by applying new technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan: include Specific Aims and Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the PHS 398-specific Research Plan, including Specific Aims and Research Strategy sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Table of Contents enumerates required PHS 398 sections (Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Vertebrate Animals, Multiple PI Leadership Plan, Bibliography & References Cited, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan). Follow page limits and content directions in the FOA and PHS 398 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the institutional environment and resources available to support the project, including laboratory space, containment level, collaborative environment, and assignment of space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions of the overall environment, assigned laboratory and office space, biosafety level(s), and local community of investigators. Describe how shared equipment and specialized cores reduce costs and support the project. Provide specifics about shared spaces and any arrangements for staff and bench assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of core facilities and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe core facilities relevant to the project (e.g., DNA Sequencing, Proteomics, Bioinformatics) including services provided, staffing, management and access/charge policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether cores perform services in-house or on a fee-for-service basis, list the Ph.D.-level scientific advisors or core managers, and describe the oversight (e.g., steering committee) and availability of consultation on experimental design and instrument capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe bioinformatics and IT infrastructure for data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Document bioinformatics resources (hardware/software), personnel, servers, storage capacity, databases, analysis pipelines, and systems administration available to support data generation and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details such as sequence alignment/assembly tools, BLAST services, microarray/statistics packages, proteomics pipelines, custom scripts, compute clusters (node specs, RAM), database servers, and network bandwidth/access to external sequencing centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment: list major and shared equipment relevant to project
rubrics_metrics.description: List laboratory and core equipment available to perform the work (e.g., biosafety cabinets, centrifuges, sequencers, real-time PCR instruments, ultracentrifuges, bioanalyzer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which instruments are shared/core-managed, how they are scheduled and overseen, and whether specialized instruments are operated by dedicated trained staff. Note access to external high-throughput sequencers (fee-for-service) if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch (Biosketch) required format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a biographical sketch for each Senior/Key person following PHS 398 instructions: NAME, POSITION TITLE, eRA COMMONS USER NAME, EDUCATION/TRAINING, A. Personal Statement, B. Positions and Honors, C. Selected peer-reviewed publications, and D. Research Support. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a Personal Statement that states the applicant's role in the project and relevant experience. Highlight the 'Most relevant to the current application' items. Follow the four-page limit strictly and include education/training start with baccalaureate, and recent and ongoing research support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach Current & Pending Support for Senior/Key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Include documentation of current and pending support (other grants) for senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List on the Senior/Key Person profile and attach supporting documents as required. This helps reviewers evaluate available effort, potential overlap, and commitment to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: Description of animals and how they will be used
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear description of the species, numbers, source, and specific procedures for how animals will be used in the project (e.g., infections, harvests, surgical procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: specify rats and mice usage, number expected over the project period, strains/vendors, infection procedures, monitoring, and endpoints. Include justification for terminal procedures and any immunosuppression methods to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: Justification for use of animals and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why animals are necessary (no suitable alternatives), why the chosen species and numbers are appropriate, and steps taken to reduce animal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale comparing in vitro vs in vivo alternatives, explain why animals provide required biological material, and describe in vitro methods used to reduce reliance on animals where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: Veterinary care, housing and institutional assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Document veterinary care arrangements, housing conditions, institutional PHS Assurance numbers, and details of animal facility oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include presence of an attending veterinarian, staffing of vivarium, sentinel monitoring, temperature/light/humidity control, PHS Assurance (OLAW) and USDA registration where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: Provisions to minimize stress, discomfort and injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe monitoring, humane endpoints, anesthesia/analgesia methods, and daily checks to minimize distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State monitoring frequency, criteria for intervention or euthanasia, anesthetic agents (e.g., ketamine/xylazine), and plans to alert veterinary staff if distress is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: Euthanasia methods and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide euthanasia methods consistent with professional guidelines (e.g., AVMA) and describe terminal procedures used during harvest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: mice euthanized by CO2 asphyxiation consistent with AVMA recommendations; terminal surgery described with anesthesia and methods to ensure death (e.g., aortic cut, diaphragm cut).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PI Leadership Plan: roles, responsibilities, and conflict resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple PIs are listed, provide a leadership plan defining contact PI, roles and areas of expertise, decision-making processes, conflict-resolution approach, supervision, and meeting frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: designate contact PI for reporting, describe division of scientific and administrative oversight (bioinformatics vs biological preparation), state that disagreements will be resolved by selecting the approach that generates the most complete and highest-quality data, and commit to regular joint lab meetings (e.g., monthly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan / Data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Resource Sharing Plan describing how data and other resources will be shared (e.g., deposition of gene-level data to public databases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: state that resulting gene-level data will be provided to GEO and TritrypDB. Describe any other data/organism/resource sharing, and follow NIH data sharing and public access policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support for collaborations and material/protocol transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters of support documenting collaborator commitments, provision of protocols/materials, and access to specialized expertise or equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a letter from the technology developer affirming provision of a detailed protocol and willingness to advise during setup. Letters should be specific about the support offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist items and required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS 398 Checklist and include required attachments such as Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, Vertebrate Animals, and any other specified attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist to ensure all PHS 398-specific components are included and properly labeled. Attach files with clear names and ensure each attachment contains the requested information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions, Patents, Program Income and Disclosure Permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose inventions and patents (for renewals), indicate program income if anticipated (amounts and sources by budget period), and answer whether the Government may disclose project title and PI contact if no award is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the relevant checklist items: inventions/patents reporting, program income details, and disclosure permission statement (Yes/No). These administrative disclosures are required on the PHS checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe Institutional Environmental Health & Safety and biosafety training
rubrics_metrics.description: Document presence of Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S) group, biosafety training for staff working with the organism, and containment level for lab space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: state that an active EH&S group provides ongoing safety training; all staff working with T. brucei receive biosafety training and lab-level training; laboratory space is BSL-2.
